chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Muthanna, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say in his sermon: 'O seeker of knowledge, it is as if nothing from the world remains except that which benefits by its goodness and harms by its evil, except for whom Allah has mercy.'
O seeker of knowledge! Let neither family nor wealth occupy you from yourself. You are, on the day you part from them, like a guest who stayed with them, then departed from them to others.
And the world and the Hereafter are like a dwelling from which you have moved to another; and what is between death and resurrection is but like a sleep you slept, then you woke up from it.
O seeker of knowledge! Proceed to your place in front of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for you will be rewarded for your deeds just as you render account; O seeker of knowledge.

key_terms.أَبُو ذَرٍّ: Abu Dharr, a prominent companion of the Prophet known for his asceticism
key_terms.كَمَا تَدِينُ تُدَانُ: As you render account, so you will be rendered account (reciprocity of deeds)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the world in the sermon of Abu Dharr regarding the seeker of knowledge?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights Abu Dharr al-Ghifani’s ascetic discourse, framing worldly attachments as temporary sojourns to prevent distraction from the ultimate return to Allah. It underscores the Shia emphasis on self-purification and the principle of 'kama tadin tudan' (you will be repaid as you have acted), urging the seeker of knowledge to prioritize eternal preparation over transient familial or material ties.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Musna, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It was so that Abu Zarr<sup>ra</sup>, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be Pleased with him<sup>ra</sup> said in a sermon, ‘O seeker of the knowledge. It is as if something from the world does not happen to be a thing except whatever it benefitted by its goodness and is harmed by its evil, except for the one Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Merciful to.
O seeker of knowledge! Neither should the family nor the wealth pre-occupy you from yourself. You are like a guest today sleeping among them, then you would be going away from them to the others;
and the world and the Hereafter are like a house you transfer from to another; and what is the death and the Resurrection except like a sleep you sleep, then you wake up from it?

O seeker of knowledge! Proceed to your place in front of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, for you would be Rewarded for your deeds just as you would reap what you have sown, O seeker of knowledge’.
en.sarwar: 18. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Muthanna from abu Basir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Abu Dhar, may Allah grant him favors, has said in his sermons, ‘O you who are found of knowledge, consider worldly things as nothing except what is beneficial in it, and its evil is harmful to people except those to whom Allah has done favors.

O you who are found of knowledge do not allow your family and property to preoccupy you so you forget all about your soul. One day you will leave them like a mere guest among them does. You then will depart to be with others.
This world and the next world are like two places to move from one to the other. Between death and resurrection, it is like a short nap after which you wake up.

O you, who are found of knowledge, send forward supplies for yourself before Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy; you will be rewarded for your knowledge. You shall reap as you sow, O you who are found of knowledge.’”
